lesson.title: "How much of the book is in each region?"
messages: Before the risk meeting: what share of the portfolio sits in each region?
The script already does this. I just want to be sure we both know what its numbers mean.
lesson.body: The weights in the file add up to 20, not 100. So "share" has to mean something more than the raw weight.

lesson.title: What `region_shares` does with the file
lesson.deeper: The total used for the percentages is the sum of the weights that are present in the file, not a fixed 100. If a holding is missing from the file, every other region's share goes up.

steps.text: It adds up the weight in each region.
It adds those totals together to get the whole book: **20**.
It divides each region by the whole book and shows it as a percentage. This is the number the PM sees.

questions.prompt: Do the three region shares always add up to 100%?
options: Only if the weights in the file add up to 100
No, they add up to the total weight
questions.why: Each region is divided by the sum of all regions, so the shares add up to 100% whatever the raw weights total (give or take rounding to one decimal).

questions.prompt: One holding in the file has a blank weight. What should the script do?
options: Quietly leave that holding out and carry on
Count it as the average weight
questions.why: `sum` skips blank values without saying anything. The holding is left out of its region and out of the whole-book total, and the shares still add up to 100%, so nothing looks wrong.

questions.prompt: the report says Europe is 45%. 45% of what?
options: Europe's weights are 45% of all the weights that are in the file.
questions.thanks: Got it: a share of what's in the file, not of a fixed 100.
questions.why: The share is Europe's total (9) divided by the total of everything in the file (20). It is not measured against 100, and it counts weight, not the number of stocks.
